features.name: counter_capitalized_word_share
features.definition: What proportion of all words across the counter-argument comments are capitalized words that are not sentence-initial?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads (malformed/missing -> null). Empty list -> null (no words). For each comment, tokenize words with re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z'’-]*", text). A token is capitalized if its first character is uppercase A-Z, excluding the standalone pronoun 'I' (and I'm/I'll/I've/I'd) and excluding tokens at the start of the comment or immediately following sentence-ending punctuation (. ! ?) or a newline. Result = total capitalized tokens across all comments / total word tokens across all comments; null if total tokens is 0. Raw mechanical text computation, no semantic filtering.

h0: counter_capitalized_word_share has no association with delta.
h1: Higher counter_capitalized_word_share is associated with higher probability of delta (OP view change).
note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view); association only. Capitalized words are a mechanical proxy for proper nouns/specific entities, not semantic entity recognition; acronyms and capitalized emphasis count, sentence-initial words excluded by heuristic. Share (length-normalized) used as the 'more' quantity; raw count not used. Comments may contain quoted text and possibly outcome announcements (e.g., delta awards); these are not filtered. Comment order/timing unknown.
